source_title: Bay City Roller can prove top of the pops in fascinating Breeders’ Cup Turf
source_excerpt:
The selection’s excellent second in the Arc de Triomphe is the best form on offer among the European challengers
T he Turf is the highlight of Saturday’s nine-race Breeders’ Cup card for European fans, with 10 of the 14-strong field trained in the UK, Ireland or France, and Bay City Roller (21.36) could be an excellent bet at around 9-1 with British bookmakers to give George Scott a first Breeders’ Cup winner at the second attempt.
Stall 13 is not ideal, but there is little obvious pace on his inside and Oisin Murphy managed to get close to the lead from a similar draw in the Arc. A strong second behind Daryz at Longchamp showed that Bay City Roller can act on a sound surface, and he is the top-rated runner in the field on Timeform’s ratings on that form.
The short straight, meanwhile, will also play to his strengths if Murphy can get across and sit handy, and then kick coming off the turn.
Keeneland 17.10: Ways And Means was nearly six lengths clear in a Grade One last time and should get a better trip from stall two than Explora, her main market rival.
Keeneland 17.48: Bacio, the front-running Nunthorpe winner, could face a battle for the lead and Billy Loughnane, on Donnacha O’Brien’s Comanche Brave , will be poised to pounce.
Keeneland 18.26: A strong pace should set things up for John Velazquez and Bracket Buster , who ran into traffic problems at Parx last time.

Take Pic to stay in focus after stable switch
The classy chaser Pic D’Orhy, already the winner of three Grade Ones and £1m in prize money, was a high-profile stable-switcher from Paul Nicholls to his former assistant, Dan Skelton, over the summer and can make an immediate contribution to the champion trainer’s title defence in the Charlie Hall Chase at Wetherby on Saturday.
Pic D’Orhy (2.55) was winless in four starts last season but was just a length-and-a-half away from a fourth Grade One success in the Ascot Chase in February, and also finished a close second on his seasonal debut in Saturday’s race 12 months ago.
The 11-year-old remains among the top-rated chasers in training and has often shown his best form when fresh, while good ground is also a positive as Pic D’Orhy tackles three miles for only the third time in his career.
